summary.text: A 14-year-old adolescent female, referred to the authors' institution with a chief complaint of localized abdominal pain, presented to the emergency department with a two-month history of abdominal pain and reported irregular menstruation for approximately one year. External genital examination showed an intact, non-imperforate, annular hymen with a normal orifice and a bluish-black mucosal bulge about 2 cm above the hymenal ring on the right side.

Suprapubic pelvic ultrasonographic evaluation showed a normally filled bladder; imaging was consistent with uterus didelphys, with a 134 × 75 × 73 mm right-sided mass compatible with hematometrocolpos, a normal left kidney and a non-visualized right kidney. Abdominal and pelvic MRI showed a normal liver, spleen, gallbladder, pancreas and adrenal glands, right renal agenesis, a hypertrophied 13 × 6 cm left kidney, normal bladder and ovaries, and a 132 × 72 × 70 mm right uterine mass; OHVIRA syndrome was diagnosed.

After the patient and her family were informed and gave written consent, she underwent surgery under general anesthesia, in which the obstructed right vaginal canal was opened without compromising the hymenal integrity and the accumulated menstrual blood was evacuated. A size 18 Fr Foley catheter was inserted to ensure complete drainage and removed on the first postoperative day; recovery was uneventful and she was discharged on the second postoperative day.
